openings.claim: A removable guide pocket with a swingable keeper may replace plate-friction retention while preserving inspection access.
openings.delta: Attack the incumbent dependence on plate friction from screw preload. Bend and drill supplied strips into boundaries contacting unmarked plate regions, carried by bolts through existing slots; add a pivoting strip keeper against lift. Set bounded free play rather than squeezing the plate. All parts must avoid the working edge and stroke clearance.
openings.prediction: Compared with the incumbent friction clamp, geometric capture should retain the spare within 1 mm even with negligible plate preload, if boundaries resist stroke loads and the keeper remains closed. The rival may also pass through incidental friction, making this comparison inconclusive. Gloved keeper release may enable removal/return within sixty seconds; neither result is established.
openings.probe: Before fabrication, check slot compatibility, support, clearance, keeper travel and accessible unmarked handling regions. Reject impossible geometry. Within eighty minutes, build at most two configurations sequentially using the same supplied parts: incumbent clamp and capture pocket. Initially allocate one twenty-stroke run and one timed removal/return check per configuration; permit at most three each within twenty observation minutes. Use the spare for the final run and thick gloves for its removal. Mark references and measure displacement. Capture testing uses negligible plate preload; record boundary contact and keeper opening alongside displacement. Passing both arrangements without differing contact/slip behavior does not establish the mechanism advantage.
assumptions: Slots accept M4 bolts and permit strip placement without carriage modification.
Supplied strip stiffness, bending accuracy and attachment stability permit total movement below 1 mm.
A captive keeper can remain closed under unspecified loads and release with supplied gloves.

assessment: Defeat: excessive play, strip deflection, keeper rotation, displacement above 1 mm, service above sixty seconds, forbidden contact/intrusion, or resource/time exhaustion. Unknown geometry and loads leave feasibility uncertain. This is an informative candidate probe only if compliant capture and comparison fit the stipulated resources; it is not deployment.

lineage.reason: Replace plate-preload dependence with geometric capture; retain the incumbent as the nearest experimental rival.

attacks.dependency: Screw preload must generate sufficient plate friction for retention.
